subject: Committed capacity proposal, capacity swap & price-safety net
messages:
From: Sam Torres <sam.torres@atlasanalytics.com>

Cc: Atlas Analytics Procurement <procurement@atlasanalytics.com>
Date: Sat, 28 Nov 2026 09:14:00 -0800
Subject: Committed capacity for Atlas POC — sizing and price sensitivity

Hi Rachel,

Thanks again for the demo last week. Quick follow up from our side as we scope the Jan–Feb POC: we expect steady traffic that would require roughly 8 A100-equivalent GPUs for peak concurrency, ~2M prompt+generation tokens/month, and burst tolerance for evaluation runs. We'd like to discuss a committed/reserved capacity option to guarantee these resources during the POC.

Two asks from procurement: 1) guidance on typical commit tenors you offer (6 vs 9 vs 12 months) tied to discounts, and 2) how you handle GPU cost moves — our procurement is sensitive to downward price adjustments (they want capture of savings or indexation) as well as protection if GPU market costs spike.

If you can share a short term sheet + a quick note on SKU swap / rebalancing (e.g., can we move reserved capacity between SKUs if our workload changes), that would be great. We need this for our budget review next week.

Thanks,
Sam
Sam Torres
Senior Platform Engineer, Atlas Analytics
procurement cc'd for contract/terms
From: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>
To: Sam Torres <sam.torres@atlasanalytics.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 28 Nov 2026 12:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Committed capacity for Atlas POC — sizing and price sensitivity

Hi Sam (and Atlas procurement),

Really appreciate the clarity — that helps. Attached is a draft term sheet (term_sheet_v1.pdf) with two pragmatic options we typically offer for POCs and initial reserved commitments:

- Option A: 6-month reserved (shorter tenor), 10% baseline discount off list; flexible monthly usage caps; limited SKU swap (up to 10% per quarter)
- Option B: 9–12 month reserved, 15%–20% discount scale depending on total committed token volume; more generous SKU swap (up to 20% per quarter) and priority burst capacity

On GPU price sensitivity — we can offer a safeguard that balances our inventory/hedge exposure and your procurement goals:
- Downward price moves (GPU cost falls): we propose a 50/50 pass-through of realized savings relative to the committed price quarterly, subject to a floor (no refunds below a 5% threshold).
- Upward cost moves: for the first 12 months we can cap customer-facing increases to 8% and then re-open for negotiation thereafter.

We can also include an explicit SKU swap clause: Atlas can reallocate up to X% of the reserved pool across compatible SKUs per quarter (we manage pool rebalancing) — we specify lead times and a minor rebalancing fee for swaps >15% in a quarter.

If you prefer, we can propose a 9-month path with a mid-term repricing review at 90 days (reprice only if GPU spot costs move more than 10%).

I'll loop in finance/op approvals as needed. Ben/Karthik — can you please confirm the discount bands and whether a 50/50 downward pass-through is acceptable or needs VP sign-off?

Sam — if the above aligns, I'll push a revised term sheet and DocuSign link for signature.

Regards,
Rachel Kim
Director, Solutions — Redwood Inference
term_sheet_v1.pdf attached

We need a go/no-go to get a revised term sheet to Atlas before their budget meeting on Tue.

Rachel — quick capacity readout: current reserved fleet is ~1,200 A100-equivalent units across regions. Typical utilization trends leave ~30% headroom on average; we run periodic rebalancing to optimize SKU mix.

Operational notes:
- We can support up to a 20% per-quarter SKU swap commitment for a new customer provided we have 4 weeks lead time for large-scale reassignments and agree on a small rebalancing fee to cover switching costs.
- Major swaps (>20%/quarter) will need capacity re-provisioning (6–8 week lead).
- For price-sensitivity clauses, recommend a 90-day mid-term repricing review so we surface GPU market moves and reconcile cost pass-throughs.

I've attached a short matrix (fleet_swap_matrix.csv) showing impact by region/sku and a scenario column for worst-case simultaneous spikes. Finance should confirm whether the proposed 50/50 downward split is acceptable operationally.

Subject: Final offer: 9-month reserved path for Atlas POC — term sheet + next steps

Hi Sam / Atlas procurement,

Thanks for the patience while we confirmed internal approvals. Summary of the finalized proposal we can put on DocuSign today:

- Tenor: 9 months reserved capacity (covers Jan–Mar POC + buffer).
- Capacity: initial reservation equivalent to 8 A100 GPUs for peak concurrency (detailed in term sheet).
- Pricing: 15% discount off list for committed capacity; volume escalator available if >2.5M tokens/month.
- SKU swap: Atlas may reallocate up to 15% of the reserved pool per quarter across compatible SKUs; rebalancing requests above that level are subject to a fee and 4-week operational lead time.
- Price-safety net: if realized GPU input costs fall more than 10% vs baseline, Redwood will pass through 50% of savings to Atlas via quarterly bill credit (floor: 5%); if GPU costs rise, customer-facing increases are capped at 8% for the first 12 months.
- Mid-term review: 90-day repricing checkpoint to reconcile realized market movement and agree on any adjustments.

Attachments: term_sheet_v2.pdf, pricing_sensitivity_summary.pdf
Related links: https://redwood.hubspot.com/deal/ATLAS-3472, DocuSign: https://docusign.com/sign/xyz123

Next steps: please review and, if acceptable, sign the DocuSign. Procurement — if you want different rebalancing limits or a longer repricing trigger, flag it and we'll see if finance can accommodate.

Best,
Rachel Kim
Director, Solutions — Redwood Inference
